questions.correctFeedback: Right — P(−ln X ≤ y) = P(X ≥ e^(−y)) = 1 − e^(−y), the exponential with rate 1.
questions.incorrectFeedback: CDF method: −ln X ≤ y exactly when X ≥ e^(−y), so F_Y(y) = 1 − e^(−y): Exp(1).

questions.stem: X has density f and Y = 3X. Then f_Y(y) equals…
questions.correctFeedback: Yes — x = y/3 and |dx/dy| = 1/3: stretching by 3 thins the density by 3.
questions.incorrectFeedback: x = y/3, |dx/dy| = 1/3, so f_Y(y) = f(y/3)/3. Stretching the axis by 3 spreads the same probability three times thinner.

questions.stem: X ~ U(−1, 1) and Y = X². P(Y ≤ 1/4) is…
questions.correctFeedback: Correct — Y ≤ 1/4 exactly when |X| ≤ 1/2, which has chance 1/2.
questions.incorrectFeedback: Turn it into an event about X: X² ≤ 1/4 means −1/2 ≤ X ≤ 1/2, chance 1/2. Taking only x = √y would give 1/4.

questions.stem: From Lesson 14: χ²₂ is the same distribution as…
questions.correctFeedback: Right — χ²₂ = Gamma(1, rate 1/2), the exponential with mean 2.
questions.incorrectFeedback: χ²ₙ = Gamma(n/2, rate 1/2); with n = 2 the shape is 1, which is the exponential with rate 1/2, mean 2.

questions.stem: A solution writes f_Y(y) = f_X(g⁻¹(y)) for an increasing g. What is missing?
questions.incorrectFeedback: It forgets the squeeze factor: f_Y(y) = f_X(g⁻¹(y)) · |dx/dy|. Without it the 'density' need not even have area 1.
